course.title: React
course.description: A complete, research-driven React course covering modern React 19 development from foundations through state architecture, Hooks, asynchronous UI, Actions, responsive rendering, DOM integration, testing, debugging, performance, architecture, security, server rendering concepts, and a real-world project.
prerequisites: Modern JavaScript fundamentals: functions, objects, arrays, modules, destructuring, async/await.
learningOutcomes: Build reusable React interfaces from components and JSX.
Model props, events, state, and composition.
Design minimal state and lift shared state appropriately.
Use core Hooks, reducers, context, refs, Effects, and custom Hooks correctly.
Build controlled forms and robust UI states.
Use Suspense, lazy loading, transitions, and deferred values.
Test observable behavior with React Testing Library.
Debug and profile with React Developer Tools and linting.
Understand React Compiler and performance measurement.
Organize larger apps with meaningful feature boundaries.
Apply client/server security boundaries and maintain patched dependencies.
Explain SSR, hydration, streaming, and React Server Components.
Build and review a realistic React application.

project.name: Project Dashboard
project.description: A realistic client-side dashboard integrating components, props, events, reducer state, controlled forms, derived filtering, list keys, responsive UI, accessibility labels, and behavior-focused tests. It intentionally does not pretend browser state is authoritative persistence or authorization.
steps: Create a React 19-compatible project.
Use createRoot and StrictMode.
Model project selection and creation with a reducer.
Keep search text as local state.
Derive filtered projects rather than duplicating state.
Use controlled form fields for project creation.
Use stable project IDs as keys.
Write behavior-focused tests.
Run tests and a production build.
Review accessibility, persistence, authorization, and deployment requirements before production use.
project.explanation: The reducer owns project collection and selection because those values change through related actions. Search text is local state and the filtered collection is derived. Child components receive data and callbacks through props. The form owns transient input state. Tests assert observable behavior. A production version would add a real data layer, server validation, authorization, persistence, error/loading states, and secure deployment practices.
